skill.name: pytorch-lightning
skill.description: Organize PyTorch deep learning projects with LightningModules, Trainer configurations, DataModules, callbacks, logging, and distributed training guidance.
skill.summary: Guides PyTorch Lightning model, trainer, data, logging, and distributed training workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: No evidence found for malicious intent, prompt injection, data exfiltration, or runtime shell behavior. The static alerts are false positives from Markdown formatting, Python imports, placeholders, localhost URLs, private IP examples, and logger key placeholders. Content hardening is recommended to show safer key and network configuration patterns.

remediation.issue: Logger examples place API key placeholders directly in constructor arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Show environment-variable or secret-manager patterns for Comet and Neptune logger credentials.

remediation.issue: The data download example uses an HTTP placeholder URL.
remediation.suggestion: Use HTTPS examples and mention checksum validation for downloaded datasets.

remediation.issue: Multi-node commands use a concrete private IP address as an example.
remediation.suggestion: Mark it as a placeholder or show MASTER_ADDR configuration through the user environment.

content.value_statement: PyTorch projects can become hard to train and scale consistently. This skill guides LightningModules, trainers, data modules, callbacks, logging, and distributed training.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to structure LightningModule methods for training, validation, testing, prediction, and optimizer setup.
Provides Trainer configuration guidance for devices, precision, callbacks, checkpoints, and fast debugging runs.
Shows LightningDataModule patterns for dataset preparation, setup stages, and reusable DataLoaders.
Summarizes callback and logger integrations for checkpoints, early stopping, TensorBoard, WandB, MLflow, Neptune, and Comet.
Compares DDP, FSDP, and DeepSpeed strategies for multi-GPU and multi-node training.
limitations: It provides examples and guidance, but it does not train models by itself.
Users must adapt templates to their datasets, model architectures, and infrastructure.
Distributed training guidance still requires correct cluster, driver, and network setup.
Logger API credentials and dataset sources must be configured securely by the user.

use_cases.title: Research Prototype Training
use_cases.description: Convert experimental PyTorch training code into a clearer Lightning project with reusable modules and reproducible Trainer settings.

use_cases.title: Production Training Pipeline
use_cases.description: Standardize data modules, checkpoints, loggers, and callbacks for repeatable model training jobs.

use_cases.title: Distributed Model Scaling
use_cases.description: Choose DDP, FSDP, or DeepSpeed settings for larger models and multi-node runs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic LightningModule
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a PyTorch LightningModule for an image classifier. Include training, validation, optimizer, and metric logging responsibilities.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Data Loading
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert my dataset preparation plan into a LightningDataModule. Include prepare_data, setup stages, and separate train, validation, and test loaders.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Training Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a Lightning Trainer configuration for two GPUs. Include checkpointing, early stopping, precision, deterministic behavior, and a fast debug mode.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Distributed Scaling
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare DDP, FSDP, and DeepSpeed for my model size and hardware. Recommend a strategy and list operational checks before launch.

output_examples.input: I need a clean structure for a new Lightning image classifier.
output: Separate model definition, step methods, optimizer setup, and logging responsibilities.
Use a Trainer configuration with checkpointing and fast development checks.
Add a DataModule when dataset setup becomes reusable across experiments.

output_examples.input: I need to scale training from one GPU to four nodes.
output_examples.output: The skill would compare distributed strategies, identify hardware and model constraints, and suggest launch settings plus network checks.

output_examples.input: I need experiment tracking for several training runs.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend a logger, metric naming plan, checkpoint monitoring metric, and credential handling approach.

best_practices: Keep model logic in LightningModule and data preparation in LightningDataModule.
Use deterministic settings and seed control when comparing experiments.
Store logger credentials outside source files and pass them through secure configuration.
anti_patterns: Do not copy placeholder API keys into committed training code.
Do not hardcode cluster addresses without documenting environment-specific replacements.
Do not mix dataset download, model logic, and Trainer setup in one file.

faq.question: Does this skill run training jobs?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and templates for users to adapt in their own environment.

faq.question: Can it help with multi-GPU training?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains DDP, FSDP, DeepSpeed, device settings, precision, and multi-node considerations.

faq.question: Does it include data pipeline guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers LightningDataModule methods, setup stages, and DataLoader organization.

faq.question: Which loggers are covered?
faq.answer: It references TensorBoard, WandB, MLflow, Neptune, Comet, and CSV logging.

faq.question: Is this only for advanced users?
faq.answer: No. It includes beginner module structure and advanced distributed training guidance.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use environment variables or secret managers. Do not commit API keys in project files.
